item.title: Control Resonant: How to Get Living Shards
item.description:
Living Shard is one of the most crucial resources in Control Resonant that helps players unlock different Aberrant forms, as well as upgrade them. There is a limited number of Living Shards available in a single playthrough of the game, so players will need to complete most of the content in their playthrough to access all Aberrant forms and maximize their damage. Here are all the sources that players can get Living Shards from.

Control Resonant: The Last Taxi Quest Walkthrough (All Locations & Solutions)

Track down all seven anomalous taxis hidden throughout the map to complete 'The Last Taxi' quest in Control Resonant.

By Ayyoun Ali

How to Get Living Shards in Control Resonant

There are a total of 28 Living Shards that players can acquire in a single playthrough of Control Resonant. Here are all the sources where these can be acquired.

Main Story Quests

Players will receive one Living Shard from each of the following main story missions.

  • Orientation
  • Welcome to Manhattan
  • Evacuation Procedures
  • Power Lines
  • Into the Sinkhole
  • Recursions and Iterations
  • The House in Distress
  • The Hedron Link
  • Sever the Hedron Links
  • Rebuild
  • Fight to the Core
  • The Incursion Fault
  • The Subway Fault
  • The Underpass Fault

Vendors

Each zone has an ice cream truck vendor that also sells Living Shards in Control Resonant . Players will need to upgrade some of them to higher levels to purchase multiple Living Shards from each one.

  • 2x Living Shards from the Downtown Vendor.
  • 1x Living Shard from Central Vendor.
  • 3x Living Shards from Evacuation Zone Vendors. (One near the main street and two from the vendor on the 15th floor of the Evac Building.)
  • 2x Living Shards from West Incursion Zone Vendor.
  • 2x Living Shards from The Park Vendor.
  • 2x Living Shards from Underpass Vendor.
  • 2x Living Shards from Unknown Vendor.

Players can start a New Game Plus playthrough of Control Resonant to get more Living Shards and unlock/upgrade the rest of Dylan's Aberrant forms.

item.title: The Witcher 3: The Sad Tale of the Grossbart Brothers Walkthrough
item.description:
The Sad Tale of the Grossbart Brothers is a secondary quest in The Witcher 3 that begins in Blandare , east of Rannvaig . Here, you will come across a bounty hunter named Djenge Frett , who asks Geralt whether he knows anything about the Grossbart brothers.

Speaking with him starts the quest, which can play out differently depending on your previous encounters and the choices you make further in the quest. Here is how to complete The Sad Tale of the Grossbart Brothers quest and get a lot of Diagrams as a reward.

The Witcher 3: All Alternate Appearances & How to Use Them

Looking to see what each character in The Witcher 3 looks like with their Alternate Appearance equipped? Look no further than here.

By Jake Fillery

How to Complete The Sad Tale of the Grossbart Brothers in The Witcher 3

During your conversation with Djenge Frett, there are two ways the quest can begin, depending on whether you have already encountered the Grossbart brothers.

If you have already found and killed the Grossbart brothers during your travels, Geralt will tell Djenge that he needs to find a new bounty because the brothers have already been dealt with. Djenge will ask Geralt to show him where their bodies are located. Once Geralt informs him, you will receive 20 Crowns as a reward. However, this interaction will not start a quest.

If you have not encountered the brothers yet, Djenge will mention that he is heading south and suggest that they might meet again someday. Once the conversation ends, travel south to the Grotto , located east of Fyresdal.

Finding Djenge Frett in the Grotto

Once you reach the Grotto, head inside and follow the path on the right to find Djenge Frett. Speak with him, and he will ask whether you want to work together to hunt down the Grossbart brothers.

If you refuse to help, Djenge will continue ahead and attempt to fight the brothers on his own. He will ultimately die, causing the quest to fail. Agree to work with him if you want to complete the quest.

Killing the Grossbart Brothers

After agreeing to help Djenge, head farther into the cave to find the three Grossbart brothers. Djenge will charge straight toward them, which can put him at risk of dying during the fight. If he dies, the quest will fail.

To prevent this, you can use Axii on Djenge to slow him down while you move ahead and engage the brothers yourself. Use Aard and Igni to damage them all and finish the three brothers. Once the brothers are dead, Djenge will reward you with 50 Crowns, completing The Sad Tale of the Grossbart Brothers.

All Notable Loot in the Grotto

You can loot the Grossbart brothers after defeating them, although they do not carry anything particularly valuable. There are also three chests in the area containing several useful items, including the following:

  • Diagram: Longclaw
  • Manuscript page: Superior Samum
  • Diagram: Nilfgaardian Guardsman's Armor
  • Manuscript page: Dancing Star
  • Diagram: Enhanced Ursine Armor

item.title: The Witcher 3: Should You Turn the Man In (Worthy of Trust)
item.description:
Worthy of Trust is a secondary quest in The Witcher 3 that begins in Skellige after you arrive at Kaer Trolde Harbor . As you explore the docks while starting the main questline in the region, you will come across a man who approaches Geralt with a request.

Speaking with him starts the quest, although you will need to wait a little before you can see how the situation develops. Here is how to complete the Worthy of Trust quest and what each choice offers.

All Contracts in The Witcher 3 (Full Checklist)

The Witcher 3 has over 30 Contracts to complete. Here's a full checklist of the quests, their locations, and the level you need to be.

By Jake Fillery

Should You Turn the Man In or Let Him Go in Worthy of Trust in The Witcher 3?

After reaching Kaer Trolde Harbor, speak with the man near the docks. He will explain that his ship was wrecked during the last storm, leaving him without the means to make the journey home.

He asks Geralt for a loan and promises to pay it back if they meet again in Novigrad. If you agree to help him, you will have to pay 150 Crowns. The conversation will then end, and you will need to wait for the next encounter.

After a day has passed, which you can speed up by meditating, travel to the area between Kaer Trolde Harbor and the Crossroads. There is a small camp here with a merchant, and you will find the same man sitting on some crates nearby.

Speak with him, and you will discover that he has taken on a new identity. After Geralt presses him about the situation, the man admits that he is a con artist. He asks Geralt not to turn him in to the jarl and promises to repay the loan with interest. You will now have three choices:

Let him go: Geralt will threaten the con man not to cheat a witcher again, warning him that they may meet another time.

Turn him in to the jarl OR Take care of him yourself : Both of these lead to a fight with the con man. Kill him to complete the quest and receive 20 Crowns. You can also loot his body to obtain 150 Crowns, Fried Meat, and a Skellige Longsword.

How to Get the Full Reward in Worthy of Trust in The Witcher 3

If you decide to let the con man go, wait another day by meditating, then travel to Fyresdal . You can find the village southeast of Fornhala or west of the Distillery .

Once there, you will encounter the man again, and this time he will have the money he promised. Speak with him to receive 200 Crowns and complete Worthy of Trust. Letting the man go earns you 200 Crowns in total after your initial 150 Crown loan, giving you 50 Crowns more than you originally lent him.

item.title: The Witcher 3: Shock Therapy Walkthrough
item.description:
Shock Therapy is a short optional quest in The Witcher 3 that takes place in Skellige . To start it, travel slightly west of Gedyneith and east of the Abandoned Sawmill . As you pass through the area, Geralt will hear a Druid calling him over. Speak with the Druid to learn more about his unusual request and begin the Shock Therapy quest.

The Witcher 3: All Missable Quests (Cutoff Points)

Find a full list of all missable side quests in The Witcher 3 (and both expansions) right here so you know the cutoff point for completing them.

By Jake Fillery

Shock Therapy Walkthrough in The Witcher 3

When you talk to the Druid, you will learn that another Druid named Egill has gone mute, and no spell or potion has managed to restore his speech. The Druid believes that strong emotions might help Egill speak again, so he asks Geralt to scare or annoy him into breaking his silence. In return for your help, he promises a Gwent card.

Once the quest begins, track it and follow the objective to find Egill, who is located nearby. You can speak to the Taciturn Druid, but none of the dialogue options will get a response from him.

Scaring Egill Three Times

To complete the quest, you need to scare Egill three times by observing what he is doing and choosing the appropriate action.

  • When Egill is lying on the mat: Look for the food pots nearby and use Aard on them. This will make Egill get up and show Geralt his middle finger.
  • When Egill is praying on the rock slab: Look around for a nearby tree stump with a hornet's nest. Use Aard to disturb the nest and interrupt his prayer.
  • When Egill is warming himself by the fire: Approach the fire and extinguish it to annoy him.

Once you have completed all three actions, Egill will kneel down and angrily tell Geralt to go away, breaking his vow of silence. Geralt will learn that Egill had been trying to maintain his vow of silence for three years, but the pranks forced him to speak again. Choose any dialogue option and return to the Druid who gave you the task.

Speak with the Druid again and choose any dialogue option to complete Shock Therapy. As a reward, you will receive some XP and the Iorveth Gwent card.

item.title: Dungeons and Dragons Teases Iconic Enemy in World of Warcraft Crossover
item.description:
Dungeons and Dragons is teasing one of World of Warcraft 's most iconic characters as an enemy, giving players a sneak preview of Illidan Stormrage. The Blizzard crossover will release as a full-fledged expansion for the 2024 edition of Dungeons and Dragons .

While Dungeons and Dragons has not featured a wealth of core crossover content, the game has recently taken note from Magic: the Gathering . Wizards of the Coast officially revealed Dungeons and Dragons ' own "Universes Beyond" initiative, bringing iconic franchises and properties into the framework of the beloved tabletop game. World of Warcraft was confirmed as the first new crossover coming to the game, while also revealing a Star Wars collaboration to come later in 2027. Now, with less than two months until the World of Warcraft crossover, Wizards of the Coast is teasing one of Blizzard's most iconic characters.

Dungeons and Dragons Reveals Eight New Subclasses and Species

Dungeons and Dragons reveals a multitude of new subclasses and species that players can select when building their characters.

By Michael Brandon Ingram

Dungeons and Dragons Teases Illidan Stormrage

A brand-new video shared by Wizards of the Coast showcases the inclusion of Illidan Stormrage in the crossover expansion. The video features several people attempting to guess D&D 's Challenge Rating for Illidan, with many of the guesses placing him above CR 20 as a powerful endgame boss. The teaser explains that Wizards of the Coast worked to adapt several of Illidan's most iconic attacks from his boss battle at the Black Temple into Dungeons and Dragons ' ruleset, striving to keep his depiction close to the fearsome original. The D&D: World of Warcraft expansion is scheduled to release on November 17.

Illidan Stormrage is just one of a wealth of beloved World of Warcraft characters coming to Dungeons and Dragons . Players will be able to square off against iconic villains like Anduin Wrynn and Lich King Arthas during their D&D journey through the realms of Azeroth, alongside beloved smaller enemies like the Murlocs. The Dungeons and Dragons expansion is adding a multitude of new classes to the game as well, bringing each of World of Warcraft 's thirteen classes to the tabletop RPG.

While Dungeons and Dragons has not featured many crossovers in the original game, the brand has expanded into plenty of other popular games. Magic: The Gathering has featured multiple Dungeons and Dragons -themed sets in the Wizards of the Coast trading card game, including Adventures in the Forgotten Realms and Commander Legends: Battle for Baldur's Gate. Popular D&D liveplay series Critical Role has also received its own adaptation into official Dungeons and Dragons content, such as The Explorer's Guide to Wildemount and Call of the Netherdeep.

Dungeons and Dragons Teases Iconic Enemy in World of Warcraft Crossover
5 Perfect Dungeons & Dragons Games Nobody Remembers
Dungeons and Dragons Reveals Eight New Subclasses and Species
5 Dungeons & Dragons Classes With Abilities Perfect for an Open-World RPG

Fans of Dungeons and Dragons should have no shortage of exciting new content on the way for the tabletop RPG. Wizards of the Coast revealed it will be bringing back the popular Dark Sun setting in 2027, featuring a mature, post-apocalyptic setting on the world of Athas. Joe Manganiello and former D&D product designer Mike Mearls also teamed up in July to debut Death Saves as an official dark fantasy campaign setting for Dungeons and Dragons . Dungeons and Dragons is teasing one of World of Warcraft 's most iconic characters as an enemy, giving players a sneak preview of Illidan Stormrage. The Blizzard crossover will release as a full-fledged expansion for the 2024 edition of Dungeons and Dragons .

While Dungeons and Dragons has not featured a wealth of core crossover content, the game has recently taken note from Magic: the Gathering . Wizards of the Coast officially revealed Dungeons and Dragons ' own "Universes Beyond" initiative, bringing iconic franchises and properties into the framework of the beloved tabletop game. World of Warcraft was confirmed as the first new crossover coming to the game, while also revealing a Star Wars collaboration to come later in 2027. Now, with less than two months until the World of Warcraft crossover, Wizards of the Coast is teasing one of Blizzard's most iconic characters.

Dungeons and Dragons Reveals Eight New Subclasses and Species

Dungeons and Dragons reveals a multitude of new subclasses and species that players can select when building their characters.

By Michael Brandon Ingram

Dungeons and Dragons Teases Illidan Stormrage

A brand-new video shared by Wizards of the Coast showcases the inclusion of Illidan Stormrage in the crossover expansion. The video features several people attempting to guess D&D 's Challenge Rating for Illidan, with many of the guesses placing him above CR 20 as a powerful endgame boss. The teaser explains that Wizards of the Coast worked to adapt several of Illidan's most iconic attacks from his boss battle at the Black Temple into Dungeons and Dragons ' ruleset, striving to keep his depiction close to the fearsome original. The D&D: World of Warcraft expansion is scheduled to release on November 17.

Illidan Stormrage is just one of a wealth of beloved World of Warcraft characters coming to Dungeons and Dragons . Players will be able to square off against iconic villains like Anduin Wrynn and Lich King Arthas during their D&D journey through the realms of Azeroth, alongside beloved smaller enemies like the Murlocs. The Dungeons and Dragons expansion is adding a multitude of new classes to the game as well, bringing each of World of Warcraft 's thirteen classes to the tabletop RPG.

While Dungeons and Dragons has not featured many crossovers in the original game, the brand has expanded into plenty of other popular games. Magic: The Gathering has featured multiple Dungeons and Dragons -themed sets in the Wizards of the Coast trading card game, including Adventures in the Forgotten Realms and Commander Legends: Battle for Baldur's Gate. Popular D&D liveplay series Critical Role has also received its own adaptation into official Dungeons and Dragons content, such as The Explorer's Guide to Wildemount and Call of the Netherdeep.

Fans of Dungeons and Dragons should have no shortage of exciting new content on the way for the tabletop RPG. Wizards of the Coast revealed it will be bringing back the popular Dark Sun setting in 2027, featuring a mature, post-apocalyptic setting on the world of Athas. Joe Manganiello and former D&D product designer Mike Mearls also teamed up in July to debut Death Saves as an official dark fantasy campaign setting for Dungeons and Dragons . Between new crossovers and settings, Dungeons and Dragons looks to expand its brand even further throughout the rest of 2026 and into 2027.
